messages:
Jamie (Support): FYI - large customer (tenant: acme-inc) reporting ~40% 5xx on /v1/generate since 09:12 UTC after today's canary. Errors are 502/504 gateway timeouts + a handful of internal 500s. Links: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/INC-176777
Priya K: looking. any correlation with the canary id? which flag rolled? :thinking_face:
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026.03.17-rc-11 started canary rollout at 09:07 UTC (slice=3%). Config diff: canary.toggle_prefetch_v2=true
Jamie (Support): user-reported sample request id: r_0a1b2c3d. Customer also says billing spikes — token accounting shows duplicate meter events for some requests.
Alex R: grabbing logs from ingress. early glance shows increased backend timeouts to model-hosts pool and repeated retries. curl repro attached below.
Jamie (Support): repro curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \ 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-7b","input":"hello"}' -v
```
Marco T: I see canary prefetched K/V cache changes landed. That feature changes prefix cache behavior and routing to fast kernels. If prefetch misroutes, backends could be overloaded with cold loads.
Priya K: confirmed the flag was globally scoped in the rollout config by mistake. It should have been seeded-scoped. Can confirm diff: `scope: global -> seed:slice` in the release plan.
Alex R: impact: with global scope, we pushed prefetched requests to a smaller subset of nodes causing CPU hot spots + upstream timeouts. That explains 502/504 wave.
Jamie (Support): customers also reported a 401 once, but looks unrelated — probably some token trimming bug in the canary sidecar. I'll keep tracking.
Priya K: recommended action: pause rollout and rollback the scope change. Can we revert config to previous commit? I can flip the flag on the control plane but need an ops confirm for rollback window.
Alex R: preparing rollback. rollback plan: 1) set canary.toggle_prefetch_v2=false globally, 2) scale up prefetch pool by +2 temporarily, 3) monitor 5xx and latency metrics. Rollback command:
```
# ops-run
redwoodctl rollout update --id 2026.03.17-rc-11 --set canary.toggle_prefetch_v2=false --confirm
```
Marco T: also disabling auto-prefetch on the fronted routing layer to stop extra load until kvcache clients stabilize: `edge-config set prefetch.enabled false`
Jamie (Support): I'll message the customer and ask for the last-failed request ids. Also opening a billing ticket to correlate duplicate meter events.
deploy-bot: Rollout paused at 09:32 UTC by Priya K (reason: spike in 5xx).
Priya K: executing flag flip now. pushing change.
Alex R: change applied. watching. initial telemetry looks promising — 5xx dropping from 42% -> 6% in 2 minutes. still keeping canary at 0%.
Marco T: we need a postmortem: root cause = mis-scoped flag + prefetch routing bug that amplifies cold-cache load. Potential mitigation: require scope gating + automated smoke on shadow traffic.
Jamie (Support): customer updated - errors subsiding. asking for ETA on full fix and refund for billing anomalies.
Priya K: will schedule a rollback verification, then we can re-run a scoped canary to validate. Follow-up: I'll open an incident postmortem doc and assign action items.
Alex R: saved commands and logs to /var/ops/incidents/1767771234. tagging SRE to run deeper correlation for duplicate billing events.
Jamie (Support): thanks all. adding #customer-facing notes and proposed refund language to the ticket. :thumbsup:
